Al-Qaeda [a] is a ___E:pan-Islamist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pan-Islamist)___ militant organization led by ___E:Sunni U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunni_Islam)___ ___E:jihadists U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jihadists)___ who self-identify as a vanguard spearheading a global ___E:Islamist revolution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revolutionary_Islamism)___ to unite the ___E:Muslim world U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muslim_world)___ under a supra-national Islamic ___E:caliphate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caliphate)___ .
Its membership is mostly composed of ___E:Arabs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab)___ but also includes people from other ethnic groups.

Al-Qaeda has mounted attacks on civilian and military targets of the U.S. and its allies; such as the ___E:1998 US embassy bombings U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_United_States_embassy_bombings)___ , the ___E:USS Cole bombing U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Cole_bombing)___ , and the ___E:September 11 attacks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/September_11_attacks)___ .

It has been ___E:designated a terrorist organization U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_designated_terrorist_groups)___ by the ___E:United Nations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations)___ and over two dozen countries around the world.

The organization was founded in a series of meetings held in ___E:Peshawar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peshawar)___ during 1988, attended by ___E:Abdullah Azzam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abdullah_Yusuf_Azzam)___ , ___E:Osama bin Laden U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osama_bin_Laden)___ , ___E:Muhammad Atef U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohammed_Atef)___ , ___E:Ayman al-Zawahiri U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayman_al-Zawahiri)___ and other veterans of the ___E:Soviet–Afghan War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet%E2%80%93Afghan_War)___ .
Building upon the networks of Maktab al-Khidamat , the founding members decided to create an organization named " Al-Qaeda " to serve as a "vanguard" for jihad .

When ___E:Saddam Hussein U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saddam_Hussein)___ ___E:invaded and occupied Kuwait U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraqi_invasion_of_Kuwait)___ in 1990, bin Laden offered to support ___E:Saudi Arabia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Arabia)___ by sending his Mujahideen fighters.
His offer was rebuffed by the Saudi government, which instead sought the aid of the ___E:United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States)___ .

The stationing of U.S. troops in the ___E:Arabian Peninsula U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabian_Peninsula)___ prompted bin Laden to declare a jihad against both the rulers of Saudi Arabia – whom he denounced as murtadd (apostates) – and against the US. From 1992, al-Qaeda established its headquarters in ___E:Sudan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudan)___ until it was expelled in 1996. It then shifted its base to the ___E:Taliban U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taliban)___ -ruled ___E:Afghanistan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_Emirate_of_Afghanistan_(1996%E2%80%932001))___ and later expanded to other parts of the world, primarily in the ___E:Middle East U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_East)___ and ___E:South Asia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Asia)___ .
In 1996 and 1998, bin Laden issued two ___E:fatāwā U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fataw%C4%81_of_Osama_bin_Laden)___ that demanded the withdrawal of U.S. troops from Saudi Arabia.

In 1998, al-Qaeda conducted the ___E:US embassy bombings U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_United_States_embassy_bombings)___ in ___E:Kenya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya)___ and ___E:Tanzania U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanzania)___ , which killed 224 people.
The U.S. retaliated by launching ___E:Operation Infinite Reach U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Infinite_Reach)___ , against al-Qaeda targets in Afghanistan and Sudan.

In 2001, al-Qaeda carried out the ___E:September 11 attacks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/September_11_attacks)___ , resulting in nearly ___E:3,000 deaths U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casualties_of_the_September_11_attacks)___ , ___E:long-term health consequences of nearby residents U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Health_effects_arising_from_the_September_11_attacks)___ , ___E:damage to global economic markets U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_effects_of_the_September_11_attacks)___ , the triggering of ___E:drastic geo-political changes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aftermath_of_the_September_11_attacks)___ as well as generating profound ___E:cultural influence across the world U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_influence_of_the_September_11_attacks)___ .

The U.S. launched the ___E:war on Terror U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_on_Terror)___ in response and ___E:invaded Afghanistan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_invasion_of_Afghanistan)___ to depose the Taliban and destroy al-Qaeda.

In 2003, a U.S.-led coalition ___E:invaded Iraq U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_invasion_of_Iraq)___ , overthrowing the ___E:Ba'athist regime U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ba%27athist_Iraq)___ which they ___E:falsely accused U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rationale_for_the_Iraq_War)___ of having ties with al-Qaeda.
In 2004, al-Qaeda launched its ___E:Iraqi regional branch U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Qaeda_in_Iraq)___ .

After ___E:pursuing him for almost a decade U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhunt_for_Osama_bin_Laden)___ , the U.S. military ___E:killed bin Laden U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Killing_of_Osama_bin_Laden)___ in ___E:Pakistan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistan)___ in May 2011.

Al-Qaeda members believe that a ___E:Judeo-Christian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judeo-Christian)___ alliance (led by the ___E:United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States)___ ) is waging a ___E:war against Islam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_on_Islam_controversy)___ and conspiring to destroy ___E:Islam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islam)___ .
Al-Qaeda also opposes ___E:man-made laws U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Man-made_law)___ , and seek to implement sharīʿah (Islamic law) in Muslim countries.

Al-Qaeda fighters characteristically deploy tactics such as ___E:suicide attacks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suicide_attack)___ ( ___E:Inghimasi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inghimasi)___ and ___E:Istishhadi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Istishhad)___ operations) involving simultaneous bombing of several ___E:targets U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Target_of_opportunity)___ in battle-zones.  ___E:Al-Qaeda's Iraq branch U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Qaeda_in_Iraq)___ , which later morphed into the ___E:Islamic State of Iraq U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_State_of_Iraq)___ after 2006, was responsible for numerous ___E:sectarian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sectarian_violence_among_Muslims)___ attacks against ___E:Shias U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shia_Islam)___ during its ___E:Iraqi insurgency U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraqi_insurgency_(2003%E2%80%932011))___ .

Al-Qaeda ideologues envision the violent removal of all foreign and ___E:secularist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secularism)___ influences in ___E:Muslim countries U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muslim_world)___ , which it denounces as corrupt deviations.
Following the death of bin Laden in 2011, al-Qaeda vowed to avenge his killing.

The group was then led by Egyptian ___E:Ayman al-Zawahiri U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayman_al-Zawahiri)___ until he too was ___E:killed by the United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Killing_of_Ayman_al-Zawahiri)___ in 2022. As of 2021 [update] , they have reportedly suffered from a deterioration of central command over its regional operations.
Al-Qaeda only indirectly controls its day-to-day operations.

Its philosophy calls for the ___E:centralization U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centralization)___ of decision making, while allowing for the ___E:decentralization U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decentralization)___ of execution.
The top leaders of al-Qaeda have defined the organization's ideology and guiding strategy, and they have also articulated simple and easy-to-receive messages.
At the same time, mid-level organizations were given autonomy, but they had to consult with top management before large-scale attacks and assassinations.
Top management included the shura council as well as committees on military operations, finance, and information sharing.
Through the information committees of al-Qaeda, Zawahiri placed special emphasis on communicating with his groups.
However, after the ___E:war on terror U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_on_terror)___ , al-Qaeda's leadership has become isolated.
As a result, the leadership has become decentralized, and the organization has become regionalized into several al-Qaeda groups.

The group was initially dominated by ___E:Egyptians U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egyptians)___ and ___E:Saudis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudis)___ , with some participation from ___E:Yemenis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yemenis)___ and ___E:Kuwaitis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuwaitis)___ .
Over time, it has evolved into a more international terrorist organization.

While its core group originally shared a background in Egypt and the Arabian Peninsula, it has since attracted fighters from other Arab groups, including ___E:North Africans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maghrebi_Arabs)___ , ___E:Jordanians U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordanians)___ , ___E:Palestinians U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinians)___ , and ___E:Iraqis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraqis)___ .

In the decade following the 9/11 attacks, Muslims from non-Arab backgrounds, such as ___E:Pakistanis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistanis)___ , ___E:Afghans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghans)___ , ___E:Turks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkish_people)___ , ___E:Kurds U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurds)___ , and ___E:European converts to Islam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islam_in_Europe)___ , have also joined the organization.
Many Western analysts do not believe that the global jihadist movement is driven at every level by al-Qaeda's leadership.
However, bin Laden held considerable ideological influence over revolutionary Islamist movements across the world.
Experts argue that al-Qaeda has fragmented into a number of disparate regional movements, and that these groups bear little connection with one another.
This view mirrors the account given by Osama bin Laden in his October 2001 interview with ___E:Tayseer Allouni U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tayseer_Allouni)___ :
"this matter isn't about any specific person and ... is not about the al-Qa'idah Organization.
We are the children of an Islamic Nation, with Prophet Muhammad as its leader, our Lord is one ... and all the true believers [mu'mineen] are brothers.

So the situation isn't like the West portrays it, that there is an 'organization' with a specific name (such as 'al-Qa'idah') and so on. That particular name is very old. It was born without any intention from us. Brother Abu Ubaida ... created a military base to train the young men to fight against the vicious, arrogant, brutal, terrorizing Soviet empire ...
So this place was called 'The Base' ['Al-Qa'idah'], as in a training base, so this name grew and became.
We aren't separated from this nation.

We are the children of a nation, and we are an inseparable part of it, and from those public demonstrations which spread from the far east, from the Philippines to Indonesia, to Malaysia, to India, to Pakistan, reaching Mauritania ... and so we discuss the conscience of this nation."
As of 2010 [update] however, ___E:Bruce Hoffman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_Hoffman)___ saw al-Qaeda as a cohesive network that was strongly led from the Pakistani tribal areas.

___E:Osama bin Laden U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osama_bin_Laden)___ served as the emir of al-Qaeda from the organization's founding in 1988 until his assassination by US forces on May 1, 2011.  ___E:Atiyah Abd al-Rahman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atiyah_Abd_al-Rahman)___ was alleged to be second in command prior to his death on August 22, 2011.
Bin Laden was advised by a ___E:Shura Council U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shura)___ , which consists of senior al-Qaeda members.
The group was estimated to consist of 20–30 people.
___E:Ayman al-Zawahiri U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayman_al-Zawahiri)___ had been al-Qaeda's deputy emir and assumed the role of emir following bin Laden's death.
Al-Zawahiri replaced ___E:Saif al-Adel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saif_al-Adel)___ , who had served as interim commander.

On June 5, 2012, Pakistani intelligence officials announced that al-Rahman's alleged successor as second in command, ___E:Abu Yahya al-Libi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Yahya_al-Libi)___ , had been killed in Pakistan.

___E:Nasir al-Wuhayshi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nasir_al-Wuhayshi)___ was alleged to have become al-Qaeda's overall second in command and general manager in 2013. He was concurrently the leader of ___E:al-Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Qaeda_in_the_Arabian_Peninsula)___ (AQAP) until he was killed by a US airstrike in Yemen in June 2015.  ___E:Abu Khayr al-Masri U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Khayr_al-Masri)___ , Wuhayshi's alleged successor as the deputy to Ayman al-Zawahiri, was killed by a US airstrike in Syria in February 2017.  Al-Qaeda's next alleged number two leader, ___E:Abdullah Ahmed Abdullah U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abdullah_Ahmed_Abdullah)___ , was killed by Israeli agents.
His pseudonym was Abu Muhammad al-Masri, who was killed in November 2020 in Iran. He was involved in the 1998 bombings of the US embassies in Kenya and Tanzania.
Al-Qaeda's network was built from scratch as a conspiratorial network which drew upon the leadership of a number of regional nodes.

Al-Zawahiri was killed on July 31, 2022, in a drone strike in Afghanistan.

In February 2023, a report from the United Nations, based on member state intelligence, concluded that de facto leadership of al-Qaeda had passed to ___E:Saif al-Adel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saif_al-Adel)___ , who was operating out of Iran. Adel, a former Egyptian army officer, became a military instructor in al-Qaeda camps in the 1990s and was known for his involvement in the Battle of Mogadishu.

The report stated that al-Adel's leadership could not officially be declared by al-Qaeda because of "political sensitivities" of ___E:Afghan government U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghan_Government)___ in acknowledging the death of Al-Zawahiri as well as due to "theological and operational" challenges posed by the location of al-Adel in ___E:Iran U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran)___ .
Most of al-Qaeda's top leaders and operational directors were veterans who fought against the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan in the 1980s.
Osama bin Laden and his deputy, Ayman al-Zawahiri, were the leaders who were considered the operational commanders of the organization.
Nevertheless, al-Qaeda was not ___E:operationally U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_operation)___ managed by Ayman al-Zawahiri.
Several operational groups exist, which consult with the leadership in situations where attacks are in preparation.  "...
Zawahiri does not claim to have direct hierarchical control over al Qaeda's vast, networked structure.
Al Qaeda's core leadership seeks to centralize the organization's messaging and strategy rather than to manage the daily operations of its franchises.

But formal affiliates are required to consult with al Qaeda's core leadership before carrying out large-scale attacks." Al-Qaeda central (AQC) is a conglomerate of expert committees, each in supervision of distinct tasks and objectives.

Its membership is mostly composed of ___E:Egyptian Islamist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islam_in_Egypt#Islamic_political_movements)___ leaders who participated in the ___E:anti-communist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-communist)___ ___E:Afghan Jihad U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghan_Jihad)___ .
Assisting them are hundreds of Islamic field operatives and commanders, based in various regions of the ___E:Muslim World U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muslim_World)___ .

The central leadership assumes control of the doctrinal approach and overall propaganda campaign; while the regional commanders were empowered with independence in military strategy and political maneuvering.
This novel hierarchy made it possible for the organisation to launch wide-range offensives.

When asked in 2005 about the possibility of al-Qaeda's connection to the ___E:July 7, 2005 London bombings U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/July_7,_2005_London_bombings)___ , ___E:Metropolitan Police Commissioner U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Police_Commissioner)___ ___E:Sir Ian Blair U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sir_Ian_Blair)___ said: "Al-Qaeda is not an organization.
Al-Qaeda is a way of working ... but this has the hallmark of that approach ...

Al-Qaeda clearly has the ability to provide training ... to provide expertise ... and I think that is what has occurred here."  On August 13, 2005, The Independent newspaper, reported that the July 7 bombers had acted independently of an al-Qaeda mastermind.

Nasser al-Bahri, who was Osama bin Laden's bodyguard for four years in the run-up to 9/11 wrote in his memoir a highly detailed description of how the group functioned at that time. Al-Bahri described al-Qaeda's formal administrative structure and vast arsenal.
However, the author ___E:Adam Curtis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Curtis)___ argued that the idea of al-Qaeda as a formal organization is primarily an American invention.

Curtis contended the name "Al-Qaeda" was first brought to the attention of the public in the 2001 trial of bin Laden and the four men accused of the ___E:1998 US embassy bombings U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_US_embassy_bombings)___ in East Africa.
Curtis wrote:
The reality was that bin Laden and Ayman al-Zawahiri had become the focus of a loose association of disillusioned Islamist militants who were attracted by the new strategy.
But there was no organization.
These were militants who mostly planned their own operations and looked to bin Laden for funding and assistance.
He was not their commander.
There is also no evidence that bin Laden used the term "al-Qaeda" to refer to the name of a group until after September 11 attacks, when he realized that this was the term the Americans had given it.

During the 2001 trial, the ___E:US Department of Justice U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Justice)___ needed to show that bin Laden was the leader of a criminal organization in order to charge him ___E:in absentia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trial_in_absentia)___ under the ___E:Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Racketeer_Influenced_and_Corrupt_Organizations_Act)___ .

The name of the organization and details of its structure were provided in the testimony of ___E:Jamal al-Fadl U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamal_al-Fadl)___ , who said he was a founding member of the group and a former employee of bin Laden.

Questions about the reliability of al-Fadl's testimony have been raised by a number of sources because of his history of dishonesty, and because he was delivering it as part of a ___E:plea bargain U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plea_bargain)___ agreement after being convicted of conspiring to attack US military establishments.
Sam Schmidt, a defense attorney who defended al-Fadl, said:
There were selective portions of al-Fadl's testimony that I believe was false, to help support the picture that he helped the Americans join together.
I think he lied in a number of specific testimony about a unified image of what this organization was. It made al-Qaeda the new Mafia or the new Communists.
It made them identifiable as a group and therefore made it easier to prosecute any person associated with al-Qaeda for any acts or statements made by bin Laden.
The number of individuals in the group who have undergone proper military training, and are capable of commanding insurgent forces, is largely unknown.

Documents captured in the raid on bin Laden's compound in 2011 show that the core al-Qaeda membership in 2002 was 170.  In 2006, it was estimated that al-Qaeda had several thousand commanders embedded in 40 countries.
As of 2009 [update] , it was believed that no more than 200–300 members were still active commanders.
According to the 2004 BBC documentary The Power of Nightmares , al-Qaeda was so weakly linked together that it was hard to say it existed apart from bin Laden and a small clique of close associates.

The lack of any significant numbers of convicted al-Qaeda members, despite a large number of arrests on terrorism charges, was cited by the documentary as a reason to doubt whether a widespread entity that met the description of al-Qaeda existed.  al-Qaeda's commanders, as well as its sleeping agents, are hiding in different parts of the world to this day. They are mainly hunted by the American and Israeli secret services.
According to author Robert Cassidy, al-Qaeda maintains two separate forces which are deployed alongside insurgents in Iraq and Pakistan.

The first, numbering in the tens of thousands, was "organized, trained, and equipped as insurgent combat forces" in the Soviet–Afghan war.  The force was composed primarily of foreign mujahideen from Saudi Arabia and Yemen.
Many of these fighters went on to fight in Bosnia and Somalia for global jihad .
Another group, which numbered 10,000 in 2006, live in the West and have received rudimentary combat training.
Other analysts have described al-Qaeda's rank and file as being "predominantly Arab" in its first years of operation, but that the organization also includes "other peoples" as of 2007 [update] .
It has been estimated that 62 percent of al-Qaeda members have a university education.
In 2011 and the following year, the Americans successfully settled accounts with Osama bin Laden, Anwar al-Awlaki, the organization's chief propagandist, and Abu Yahya al-Libi's deputy commander.
The optimistic voices were already saying it was over for al-Qaeda.
Nevertheless, it was around this time that the Arab Spring greeted the region, the turmoil of which came great to al-Qaeda's regional forces.
Seven years later, Ayman al-Zawahiri became arguably the number one leader in the organization, implementing his strategy with systematic consistency.

Tens of thousands loyal to al-Qaeda and related organizations were able to challenge local and regional stability and ruthlessly attack their enemies in the Middle East, Africa, South Asia, Southeast Asia, Europe and Russia alike.
In fact, from Northwest Africa to South Asia, al-Qaeda had more than two dozen "franchise-based" allies.
The number of al-Qaeda militants was set at 20,000 in Syria alone, and they had 4,000 members in Yemen and about 7,000 in Somalia.
The war was not over.
In 2001, al-Qaeda had around 20 functioning cells and 70,000 insurgents spread over sixty nations.
According to latest estimates, the number of active-duty soldiers under its command and allied militias have risen to approximately 250,000 by 2018.
Al-Qaeda usually does not disburse funds for attacks, and very rarely makes wire transfers.
In the 1990s, financing came partly from the personal wealth of Osama bin Laden.

Other sources of income included the ___E:heroin trade U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heroin_trade)___ and donations from supporters in Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and other Islamic ___E:Gulf states U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab_states_of_the_Persian_Gulf)___ .
A 2009 ___E:leaked diplomatic cable U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_diplomatic_cables_leak)___ stated that "terrorist funding emanating from Saudi Arabia remains a serious concern."

Among the first pieces of evidence regarding Saudi Arabia's support for al-Qaeda was the so-called " ___E:Golden Chain U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Golden_Chain)___ ", a list of early al-Qaeda funders seized during a 2002 raid in Sarajevo by Bosnian police.
The hand-written list was validated by al-Qaeda defector Jamal al-Fadl, and included the names of both donors and beneficiaries.
Osama bin-Laden's name appeared seven times among the beneficiaries, while 20 Saudi and Gulf-based businessmen and politicians were listed among the donors.
